store: cmos/db/cmos.sqlite, read with sqlite3 -readonly; nothing written

id.note: The record identity. CMOS uses an integer; the object declares a string so the same object can carry another store's ids.

context_id.reason: One value ("master_context") on every row: a CMOS partition key with no design meaning.

decision_text.note: The decision itself, and the sprint's long-free-text risk: 61 to 8,418 characters, 197 rows over 2,000.

sprint_id.note: The link to Sprint; every non-null value resolves against sprints.id, 0 dangling.

snapshot_id.reason: CMOS context-snapshot pointer, null on 1,868 of 1,933 rows; internal bookkeeping.

mission_id.note: The mission that captured it. Stored loosely in CMOS (often a bare "m02" rather than "s203-m02"), so it is shown as a label, never as a resolved link.

category.note: Sparse in practice (1,928 of 1,933 null, 6 distinct values including null), so the screen must read correctly when it is absent.

superseded_by.note: The self-referencing lineage pointer. Populated on exactly the 45 rows whose status is superseded — a clean 1:1.

status.note: active | superseded | archived | stale is the supersession lifecycle, not a generic workflow, so Supersedable owns it rather than Stateful.

evidence.note: An array of {type, id} references. Sparse (1,923 of 1,933 null) but real, and it is what m05 will show beside a design.

content_hash.reason: CMOS de-duplication hash, null on 889 rows; internal bookkeeping.

last_reviewed_at.reason: Entirely null across all 1,933 rows: the staleness-review date has never been written, so there is nothing to show.

project_id.note: The project scope. A slug ("forge"), never a uuid — which is one of the reasons research/Mission cannot be reused.

stable_event_id.reason: CMOS replication envelope: the event id that carries this row between stores.

occurred_at.reason: CMOS replication envelope: the event clock, not a date the record shows.

event_type.reason: CMOS replication envelope: one value across every row of the table.

schema_version.reason: CMOS replication envelope: the row format version.

author_user_id.reason: Declared but entirely null in the live store, so there is no owner to render; Ownerable is not composed on a field that has never been written.

last_embedded_hash.reason: CMOS embedding bookkeeping for its vector index.

id.note: Heterogeneous in the live store ("Sprint 22" beside "sprint-203"), so it is treated as an opaque identifier and never parsed.

focus.note: The sprint's stated purpose; present on all 186 rows and long free text.

status.note: Active | Completed | Archived | Reverted, measured from the live store. Reverted has no counterpart in any existing object's state set and is why the states are declared here rather than borrowed.

end_date.note: Null on 47 rows, and not always a date: some rows carry a full timestamp.

total_missions.reason: Null on 176 of 186 rows. The real count is the missions table, so a screen that showed this counter would be blank or wrong almost always; Sprint carries mission_count as a derived field instead.

completed_missions.reason: Null on 177 of 186 rows, for the same reason.

author_user_id.reason: Declared but entirely null in the live store, so there is no owner to render; Ownerable is not composed on a field that has never been written.

type.note: review | planning | custom | check-in | research, measured from the live store — a classification, not a lifecycle.

title.note: The display label; present on all 499 rows.

sprint_id.note: The link to Sprint; 301 resolve, 0 dangling, 198 null.

agent.note: Which agent held the session (assistant, codex, claude-opus-5, ...). No existing object models the actor as a non-user agent.

summary.note: Long free text, present on all 499 rows.

status.note: Every one of the 499 rows is "completed"; the state set is declared from what CMOS can write, not from what the rows happen to show.

captures.note: An array of {timestamp, category, content}: what the session recorded as it ran.

next_steps.note: The same shape; null on 45 rows.

missions.reason: No screen in this sprint needs a standalone CMOS mission, and the registry is keyed by object name, so a second object named Mission cannot exist beside TraceLab's research/Mission. A CMOS mission reaches the screens this sprint builds as Sprint's derived mission_count and as the mission_id a Decision names. The reuse test against research/Mission is recorded under reuseProof and it fails.
